content: Cross-checked via GitHub issues (bitwarden/clients #7436, #14720, #13252) + scotthelme blog + Bitwarden contributing docs: no browser API lets an extension add a passkey provider alongside native WebAuthn - the only mechanism is full replacement of navigator.credentials.create/get via MAIN-world injection. Confirmed real conflicts: Bitwarden fails to prompt for passkeys when 1Password extension is also installed even with 1P passkey features disabled; Bitwarden's patch has broken non-WebAuthn page functionality (EtherPad). Separately, 1Password's wrapper had a real vulnerability: it did direct property assignment onto live navigator.credentials and only checked publicKey.hints, never the page's actual Permissions-Policy, so it could broker passkey ceremonies on pages that had explicitly disabled publickey-credentials-create via Permissions-Policy - because the wrapper runs in the page's MAIN world it's also reachable/overridable by attacker JS in that same world.
